summary: No path forgets a signed claim until its batch is older than the freshness window and a day (8 days). A copy of a signature carried within the window is caught only while every member still holds the original. Local trim, closed-mail retirement and any other forget now keep signed claims that long, and the shared deletion refuses a younger one outright.

replay.detail: No replay and no scan. The local cut lists the claims it could drop that are younger than the bound, keeps those that carry a signature, and a later day's cut takes them. Mail retirement's cutoff is a week after the close or the bound, whichever is longer.

schema.detail: No table, column, index, trigger, kind, digest or storage version change. One constant: principal::FORGET_SIGNED_AFTER_MS, the 7-day freshness window plus a day.

rules.detail: checkpoint::delete_dropped_rows_tx, through which every forget runs (local trim and its sweep, checkpoint tombstones, mail retirement), refuses the whole deletion if it would forget a signed claim whose batch is younger than 8 days. It never drops part of one. Batches timed before 2026-11-24 (the cutover less the window) are forgotten as before. The local cut keeps signed claims inside the bound and keeps its day-by-day steps; a later day's cut takes them. Closed mail now retires 8 days after its close instead of 7.

compatibility.detail: No wire, digest or capability change; peers of any version are unaffected. A member on an older build can forget signed claims sooner, so until every member runs this, a copy within the window can still read differently on it, as the freshness window's own release note says.

manual.detail: Nothing to do. Signed trim-kind claims (observations) now stay 8 days by batch time before the local cut takes them, where it took them after about a day before; closed mail stays a day longer. Measured on a real member: the trim-kind claims between 1 and 8 days old were 5,127 claims with about 14 MB of bodies, about 0.02% of the file. That is what the bound keeps longer.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to the previous release is supported; it forgets on its own schedule again.
